resources.string: Capabilities the new engine added. All of them are off until you turn them on.

Builds a second MASQUE tunnel through the first, so the site you open is reached from a different edge than the one your network saw. Slower, and much harder to tie back to you — the MASQUE equivalent of gool.
Only applies to MASQUE. With WireGuard or gool selected this stays idle — use gool for a second WireGuard hop.
The edge this device connects to. Leave blank to let the scanner choose.
The edge reached through the first one. Leave blank to let the scanner choose.
Negotiates QUIC v2 on the first packet, which passes filters that recognise and drop QUIC v1. Leave it on unless your network blocks v2 specifically.
The engine connects without Tor. Use the Chain page if you want the app\'s own Tor core instead.
WARP first, Tor through it. Works with any transport, including WireGuard.
WARP is reached from a Tor exit, so your network never sees WARP at all. Forces MASQUE over HTTP/2 — Tor carries TCP only, so WireGuard and gool are unavailable here.
Plain Tor with no WARP. Useful for checking whether the Tor half works on this network before adding anything to it.

Unavailable while a Tor chain mode is selected on the Chain page: that runs the app\'s own Tor core, and two Tor instances would fight over the same bootstrap. Set the chain back to Aether to use the engine\'s Tor.
Requires an engine built with Tor support. A build without it reports the rejected option in Diagnostics — the app\'s own Tor chain modes work on every build.
Try public relays first and fall back to bridges fetched automatically when they are blocked. Right almost everywhere.
Skip the direct attempt and start with bridges. Saves about a minute on a network that is known to block Tor.
Public relays only. On a filtered network this usually means Tor never finishes starting.
Use the bridge lines below. Leave them empty to reuse the bridges already configured on the Bridges page.
One per line, up to 8. Treat them as private: a bridge in a screenshot is a bridge that can be blocked.
Two-letter code. Asks for bridges known to work from that country.
Second local SOCKS5 port, Tor-only, on 127.0.0.1. Blank uses the engine default.
Marks the engine\'s own sockets so a tunnel front end can route around them instead of looping them back in. Needs root or CAP_NET_ADMIN — leave blank on a normal device.
Limits the new engine accepts for itself. Blank means it sizes them from the device.
Cap on proxy connections served at once. The engine picks between 512 and 8192 from the device\'s limits; raise it only if apps stall while the tunnel is idle.
Lower values free dead connections sooner on a flaky mobile link; higher ones keep long-lived sessions alive through a bad minute.
